comment: The steak frites is the best in Westlands and I will argue about it. Booked at seven, seated at seven.
Lovely room, slightly slow on a full Friday. Worth it for the onion soup.
ownerReply: Thank you Daniel. We have added a second section server on Fridays since.

comment: Sat at the counter for the omakase. Twelve pieces, not one of them ordinary.
Expensive and completely worth it. Book early, there are only sixteen seats.
Came with eight people on a Saturday and the table was ready. That never happens.
Goat was excellent, ugali could have been hotter. Kachumbari on point.
Loud, smoky, exactly what you want on a Sunday afternoon.
Proper leopard spotting on the crust. The diavola with the chilli honey is dangerous.
Pizza was great but we waited forty minutes past our booking.
ownerReply: That is not our standard and we are sorry. Please get in touch, we would like to make it right.

comment: The whole tilapia is a religious experience. Go hungry.
Busy, loud, and the fish arrives when it arrives. Booking through the app meant we actually had a table.
Dal makhani tastes like someone left it on overnight, because they did.
Great butter chicken. Ask for the naan to come out last, ours arrived early and went cold.
Injera made in house and you can taste the difference. The coffee ceremony is worth staying for.
Biryani close to what I grew up with in Mombasa. High praise from me.
Dim sum until three is a real commitment and they keep it. Har gow were excellent.
They nixtamalise their own corn. In Nairobi. The al pastor is the one to get.
Mezze for two easily feeds three. The lamb shish came off the charcoal perfectly.
Shakshuka and good coffee in a garden. Gets busy from nine on a Saturday, book ahead.
